search_log.query: British Museum BM 21946 Babylonian Chronicle Carchemish
search_log.notes: Museum details via Wikipedia; BM collection page not fetched.

archaeology.not_applicable_reason: Excavation evidence from Carchemish was not searched this session; the documentary record is decisive for the battle itself.

astronomy.not_applicable_reason: Absolute dating of the regnal year relies on astronomical texts via Parker & Dubberstein (not consulted directly).

claims.statement: Nebuchadnezzar defeated the Egyptian army at Carchemish in 605 BC.
claims.reasoning: The Babylonian Chronicle (ABC 5), a near-contemporary cuneiform record, directly reports the battle in Nabopolassar's 21st year. Berossus independently recalls the campaign. Jeremiah 46:2 names the same battle.
limitations: Translation read via Livius, not the printed edition.

claims.statement: Jeremiah 46:2's dating of the battle to Jehoiakim's fourth year is consistent with the Babylonian date.
claims.reasoning: Chronology engine, 32 reckoning combinations (20 consistent with the anchors: Jehoiakim's accession 1 Aug 609 – 31 Jan 608; Carchemish Mar 605 BC – Aug 605 BC). Jeremiah 46:2 ("fourth year" = Carchemish) is consistent with: accession year · Nisan; accession year · Tishri; non-accession year · Tishri; it is inconsistent with non-accession year · Nisan. Window of Daniel's "third year" by reckoning (including uncertainty): accession year · Nisan: Feb 606 BC – May 605 BC (closes before the latest possible battle date, Aug 605); accession year · Tishri: Aug 607 BC – Nov 605 BC (extends past the battle into the post-Carchemish campaign); non-accession year · Tishri: Aug 608 BC – Nov 606 BC (closes before the latest possible battle date, Aug 605); non-accession year · Nisan: Feb 607 BC – May 606 BC (closes before the latest possible battle date, Aug 605). Only accession-year counting with a Tishri (autumn) new year makes the "third year" run through the summer-605 campaign after Carchemish; accession-year counting with a Nisan (Babylonian) new year ends the "third year" around Nisan 605, before the battle except at the uncertainty margin.
limitations: Nisan/Tishri windows are conservative approximations (Parker & Dubberstein not imported).
Jehoiakim's accession window is a reconstruction.

evidence.finding: The chronicle records that in Nabopolassar's 21st year the crown prince Nebuchadnezzar crossed the Euphrates, defeated the Egyptian army at Carchemish and pursued its survivors into the district of Hamath.
Berossus (via Josephus) describes Nebuchadnezzar, sent by his father against a rebel governor in the west, defeating him and reducing the country, when news of Nabopolassar's death recalled him.
limitations: Berossus wrote c. 290 BC and survives only in quotation; he does not name Carchemish.

evidence.finding: The Egyptian army's Harran campaign of Du'ûzu–Ulûlu 609 bounds the date of Josiah's death and hence Jehoiakim's accession.

research_gaps: Carchemish excavation reports were not consulted.
Exact Nisan 1, 605 not taken from Parker & Dubberstein.
